analysis: Colorado has opened the season 2-0-0 and comes from a dominant 6-1 win over St. Louis. The Avalanche finished 2025/26 with 121 points, 39 more than Winnipeg, while Nathan MacKinnon has already started the new campaign with five points.

The 2025/26 head-to-head finished 2-2, but Winnipeg now plays without Connor Hellebuyck. Colorado arrives with the stronger recent performance, the higher offensive ceiling and a clear advantage based on last season's overall level.

Edmonton enters with the stronger high-end offensive core and has already shown it can win without needing a shootout, beating Seattle 3-1. Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl remain capable of deciding close games even when Edmonton is not at full strength.

Anaheim has started well but Troy Terry is unavailable, while Edmonton is missing Zach Hyman and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins. Those absences make the moneyline more attractive than a high total: Edmonton can cover this selection through a controlled 3-1 or 3-2 type of game.
